reviews.solutionVi: Rxg5 — Xe đen từ d5 bắt tốt ở g5. Tốt trắng f4 không thể bắt lại vì sẽ để Xe f8 chiếu Vua f3. Nếu Trắng đẩy a7, trong phương án phân tích Đen có thể đáp Ra5 để tấn công tốt thông.
hintsVi: Xe đen f8 và Vua trắng f3 nằm trên cùng một cột.
Nếu Xe d5 bắt ở g5, tốt f4 có thể bắt lại không?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rf8 pins f4 to Kf3. Without the pinner fxg5 wins the rook for a pawn, and Kxg5 recovers only one pawn (-300 cp overall).
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 27 roots compared. No mate in one or forced mate in two. Rxf4+ Kxf4 loses the rook. Kf5 permits a7 and requires many turns to gain material in deeper analysis. Rd4 and Rdf5 similarly require delayed captures or checks.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 22 legal replies preserve +100 cp immediately, and neither rook is offered. Supplemental 900k evidence after Rc6+ Kh5 Rb6 Ra5 and a7 Ra5 Rb7 Ra8 shows the passer can be contained without losing the net pawn. Apparent later recovery on b4 is offset by taking the a-pawn. Kf5 after Rc6+ is avoided because it unpins f4 and allows fxg5.
reviewNotes.level: One direct capture without preparation or sacrifice. The passer response is an ordinary rook manoeuvre after the gain.
reviewNotes.provenance: Lukasiewicz–Gibala, 40th Voivoda Cup IM 2026, checksummed TWIC 1644. Exact ply 105 after Rxc7 verified. Rxg5 was played; a7 Ra5 is analysis.

reviews.reason: Nxb3 wins the pawn because the knight on d2 is pinned. The other rook can recapture on d2 later, but the solver’s bishop and knight cover that square together and the material gain survives the ordinary exchanges.
reviews.distinctness: Both knights can reach b3. The c5 knight can take only because the other one is pinned by a bishop. Unlike Akobian–Boyer, the defender also has a rook on the pin target’s file and can trade through d2. This makes the capture an example of cooperation through multiple ordinary recaptures.
reviews.solutionVi: Nxb3 — Mã từ c5 bắt tốt ở b3. Tượng b4 ghim Mã d2 vào Vua e1, nên Trắng không thể đáp Nxb3.
hintsVi: Cả hai Mã đều có thể nhảy tới b3 theo cách đi của quân Mã. Mã nào đang bị ghim?
Hãy nhìn đường chéo b4–e1 trước khi xét nước bắt lại trên b3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Removing Bb4 makes White’s Nxb3 legal. The black pawn gain changes from +100 cp to −220 cp and there is no capture on the next Black turn.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 37 roots compared. d4 exd4 Nxb3 is an even pawn transaction at that stage. Rd8 Ke2 delays the same pin mechanism. Bxd2+ Kxd2 Nxb3+ requires an exchange and two solver moves and has a much weaker root assessment. No positive mate lead.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 22 legal replies retain +100 cp immediately. Neither the knight b3 nor bishop b4 can be captured. In 1M-node analysis after Ke2, Bxd2 Rxd2 Nxd2 Kxd2 retains +270 cp. After the played e4 dxe4 Bc4, supplemental Nxd2 and Bxd2+ lines retain +200 cp after settlement. Deep reviews of h4, Bd6, Be5 and Rg1 also preserve material through ordinary exchanges.
reviewNotes.level: A. A single direct non-sacrificial pawn capture in an almost balanced position. The defenders’ exchanges on d2 occur later and do not form a prerequisite.
reviewNotes.provenance: Banawa–Begunov, Titled Tue, 2025-10-14. Complete TWIC 1615 replay reaches 16.Rd1 at ply 31. The game played 16...Nxb3. IM White and FM Black in archive headers, checksum verified.

reviews.reason: From balanced material, the queen holds the white rook on the diagonal so the black rook can take the pawn in one move. The superficially equivalent bishop capture lets White release the pin and win the bishop through a forcing sequence.
reviews.distinctness: Published Megaranto–Avirat Chauhan Rxd4 uses a queen pin on a bishop along a file. Here the pinned defender is a rook on the same file as the target, so the learner must distinguish between two black pieces that can take the pawn and keep the rook safe after a bishop attack.
reviews.solutionVi: Rxd4 — Xe Đen từ d8 bắt tốt d4. Hậu e4 ghim Xe d3 vào Vua b1, nên Trắng không thể bắt lại bằng Rxd4. Trong ván đấu, sau Be3 tấn công Xe, Đen chuyển Xe lên d5.
hintsVi: Tìm đường chéo từ Hậu e4 đến Vua b1. Xe Trắng nào đang che đường chiếu?
Xét nước bắt tốt d4 bằng Xe và kiểm tra xem Xe d3 có thể bắt lại không.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Qe4 pins Rd3 to Kb1. Removing the pinner permits the sequence Rxd4 Bxd4 Qxd4. Black is down 400 cp after the rook recapture, temporarily back up 100 cp after the bishop takes, and finally down 230 cp when the white queen recaptures. The immediate equal rook exchange is illusory because the bishop can be taken.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 44 legal roots compared and no mate within three. Bxd4 initially wins the pawn under the same pin, but Ka1 unpins with a tactical threat and every tested strong defence for Black loses material. For example Rc4 Be3 f6 Bxd4 leaves Black down 230 cp from the start. Qxd4 Rxd4 loses the queen for a pawn.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 27 immediate replies are non-captures, so neither rook nor queen is offered. Be3 Rd5 is the original answer and retains the pawn in the deeper continuation. Qe3 Qf5 keeps the pin on d3 along the same diagonal, and Ka1 Rxd3 Rxd3 exchanges rooks while retaining the pawn.
reviewNotes.level: A direct one-move gain without a sacrifice. The strongest bishop attack requires only a rook retreat after the gain.
reviewNotes.provenance: Atanasov–Khodko, 3rd 3-0 Thu 26th Mar 2026, checksum-bound complete TWIC 1638 game. Exact ply 47 after Kb1. Rxd4 Be3 Rd5 was played.

reviews.reason: The capture wins a pawn from a balanced endgame. The king’s release of the pin can concede a second pawn in a routine rook exchange.
reviews.distinctness: A rook pins a pawn along the seventh rank so the bishop can win a pawn. The freed f-pawn can immediately be captured a second time if the king unpins it, without giving up material in the rook trade.
reviews.solutionVi: Bxg6 — Tượng trắng từ c2 bắt tốt ở g6. Xe h7 ghim tốt f7 vào Vua e7, nên Đen không thể đáp fxg6. Nếu Vua đen đi Kd6, Trắng có thể thắng thêm tốt f7 qua phương án Rxf7 Rxf7 Bxf7.
hintsVi: Nhìn hàng 7 từ Xe h7 qua tốt f7 đến Vua e7.
Tượng c2 có thể bắt ở g6 mà tốt f7 không được phép bắt lại không?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Without Rh7, ...fxg6 is legal and captures the bishop. On the real board f7 shields Ke7 from check.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 31 starting moves compared. Bxa4 Bxa4 Rxa4 looks like a simple pawn win, but ...Rb3 e4 dxe4 leads to recovery and is evaluated near equal. Ke5 is slower and needs subsequent play; Rxf7+ Kxf7 drops the exchange.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 24 replies preserve at least +100 immediately and neither participant is offered. After ...Kd6 the straightforward Rxf7 Rxf7 Bxf7 wins a second pawn through an equal rook trade. In the source ...Be8 Bxf7 Bxf7 g6 lets the passed pawn advance; the lesson only needs the initial gain.
reviewNotes.level: One direct pawn capture, with no sacrifice. The illustrative follow-up is an equal rook exchange after the initial gain.
reviewNotes.provenance: Andreikin–Esipenko, Titled Tue 2 Dec 2025, checksummed complete TWIC 1622. Exact ply 84 after ...Rxb6. 43.Bxg6 was played, with ...Be8 the actual reply.

reviews.reason: The two bishops coordinate to win the central pawn in one move from balanced material. The original defence releases the knight and attacks the capturing bishop with the king, but the bishop reaches a safe square.
reviews.distinctness: Published Bxd5 from Rasulov–Dirikolu takes a knight while a rook pins a pawn. Here one bishop pins a knight and the other takes a pawn. The opposing king can immediately step out of the pin and attack d5.
reviews.solutionVi: Bxd5 — Tượng Đen từ b7 bắt tốt d5. Tượng h6 ghim Mã f4 vào Vua e3, nên Trắng không thể đáp Nxd5. Trong ván đấu, sau Kd4 tháo ghim và tấn công Tượng, Đen chuyển Tượng sang e4, ô được Vua f5 bảo vệ.
hintsVi: Tượng h6, Mã f4 và Vua e3 cùng nằm trên đường chéo nào?
Nếu Tượng b7 bắt tốt d5, Mã f4 có thể rời đường chéo để bắt lại không?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Bh6 pins Nf4 to Ke3. Removing Bh6 makes Nxd5 legal and leaves Black down 230 cp from the adjusted start with no immediate retake.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 15 legal roots checked and no mate within three. Bxf4+ Nxf4 only trades a bishop for a knight. c5 dxc6 Bxc6 merely exchanges pawns, and only Bxd5 settles the material objective within the exact three-turn local horizon.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 14 immediate responses are non-captures. Kd4 Be4 is the played safe retreat, and targeted Bf7 also retains the gain. On a4, Be4 axb5 axb5 immediately restores the same pawn margin and the deeper line wins the knight. Neither bishop is offered as a sacrifice.
reviewNotes.level: One direct capture. The bishop move after the king unpins is an ordinary retreat after the gain.
reviewNotes.provenance: Mahdavi–Sonis, 1st 3-0 Thu 5th Feb 2026, complete checksum-bound TWIC 1631 game. Exact ply 99 after Nd3. Bxd5 Kd4 Be4 was played.

reviews.reason: An absolutely pinned pawn allows a rook to remove the central knight immediately and survive counterchecks.
reviews.distinctness: A long queen diagonal pins the pawn in a queen-versus-two-rooks endgame. White’s active rook checks are a real defence to account for, unlike the more static rook-wins-knight examples.
reviews.solutionVi: Rxe5 — Xe đen từ h5 bắt Mã ở e5. Hậu a7 ghim tốt d4 vào Vua g1, nên Trắng không thể đáp dxe5. Nếu Trắng chiếu bằng Rh4+, Đen có thể đưa Vua đến g6 và giữ được Mã vừa thắng.
hintsVi: Theo dõi đường chéo a7–g1. Quân nào đang che đường chiếu của Hậu đen?
Nếu Xe h5 bắt Mã e5, tốt d4 có được phép bắt lại không?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Removing Qa7 permits dxe5, making a nominal knight gain an exchange loss. The d-pawn shields Kg1 on the real board.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 23 legal roots compared, with no positive mate root. Qb8 and Qb6 let White seize the initiative with checking moves and do not win a piece; Qxd4+ Rxd4 loses the queen.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 26 legal replies retain at least +320 immediately. Neither piece is offered. After Rh4+ Kg6 or Rgf4 Re7, the strong probes retain the knight gain. Rf7+ Qxf7 dxe5 is an even rook exchange and retains the initial net gain. Played Rf3 Rh5 avoids recovery.
reviewNotes.level: One direct capture without a sacrifice or preparation. Counterchecks are met with a king move or an even trade.
reviewNotes.provenance: Mekhitarian–Deac, 2nd 3-0 Thu 29 Jan 2026, checksummed complete TWIC 1630. Exact ply 83 after Rg4, followed by 42...Rxe5 43.Rf3 Rh5 in the game.

exclusions.reason: The g-file pin exists but does not create the material payoff. With the g6 pawn unpinned, 34.exf5 gxf5 still gains a bishop for a pawn (+230 cp), and 35.Rxf5 keeps at least that gain even against ...Rxc3. The more costly rook capture as a root therefore also has a simpler bypass.

The nominal pawn gain is not securely retained. After Nxe4 Re3 f5 Ra3 Nc5 Kc1 e4 Bxa4, White restores the starting material, and strongest Rf3 and Rd3 lines also allow Bxa4. Black already has a decisive positional advantage before the lesson. Without Rh2, Bxe4 does refute the capture, but the pin is insufficient for the advertised material payoff.

Pin on Bd1 prevents Bxe2, but Kxe2 is legal and leaves the same +180 cp exchange win. With Bd1 unpinned, the hypothetical Bxe2 also leaves +180 cp without another capture. The motif is incidental to the stated material payoff.
After hypothetical Bxb5 Black would still have gained a rook for a pawn (+400 cp). The pin prevents a pawn recapture but is incidental to the larger material win.

The pin is incidental to the material objective. Removing the pinner a3 allows Nxf5, but exf5 still gains bishop for pawn (+230 cp). The independent Bxd6+ first removes the defender and exf5 then secures at least +320 cp through every legal Black reply to the check, including Kxd6 and cxd6. Both strongest recaptures were checked with 500k-node probes.

The c6 knight is pinned, but the hypothetical Nxd8 leaves the same +570 cp initial queen-for-bishop gain as either legal Kxd8 or Rxd8. The pin is incidental to the capture, and ...Nxc3 bxc3 Bxc3+ Nd2 Bxa1 starts real material recovery in a complex middlegame.

The passed pawn supplies a competing simple route. g7 Ke7 g8=Q Nxf1 gains three pawns nominally through promotion even after losing the rook; the game does not present a clean unique pin-creation decision.
Bxg3+ Bxg3 Rxf1 settles a net +320 cp before possible pawn recovery and still secures at least +220 cp at the short horizon. This checking bypass removes the knight instead of relying on the pin.

The direct bishop capture only wins a pawn immediately. The strong d2 passer requires substantial play and can recover the material: Bxc6 d2 Nxd2 Rxd2 Rxb7+ Rxb7 Bxb7 leaves White 20 cp below the starting material difference in the deeper defence probe. No Level A one-move material settlement shown.
The nominal gain after hypothetical Bxc5 is a knight for a pawn (+220 cp), exactly the same as the legal ...Rxc5 recovery. The pin on Bf8 is not essential to that gain.

The pin is incidental to the stated pawn gain. Without the a4 bishop, ...Nxd4 is legal but 9.Qxd4 regains the knight and retains the full nominal pawn gain. Actual ...Bd6 also requires an advanced forcing line after Nxc6 Bxh2+ Kh1 Qh4, unsuited to direct level A.

Rf3 creates a real pin and permits a pawn capture, but Black is already a rook for two pawns ahead. Roughly 19 quiet first moves retain comparable or better evaluations; the deeper best lines after ...Kg2 or ...Kh4 usually postpone or skip the pawn capture. Targeted captures still retain the pawn, but this is routine collection of additional material in an already clearly won conversion.

Ba4 really pins Nb5, but the practical decision hinges on the passed pawns. Against the strongest ...c2, the engine abandons the knight capture to play Bxc2 before the pawn promotes. Proving Bxb5+ remains suitable then requires a promotion race. The competing Bc2 immediately blocks the passer and already wins with e6/f6 pawns (+840 cp versus +849), so this is not a clean introductory material-pin exercise.

After Bxd4 Nxd4 exd4 in the counterfactual without Bd5, Black retains +90 cp material, a pawn after a nominally equal bishop-for-knight exchange. The stronger exd4 also wins at least the pawn without the pin, and Nxd4 Bxd4 would cost White a knight (+320 cp), with no direct White recapture. The pin is incidental to the stated pawn gain.

The pin is incidental to the one-move material claim. On the exact counterfactual board without Qc5, ...Bxc6 Nxc6 bxc6 leaves Black up one minor piece, essentially the same gain as ...Bxc6 without a reply. The pinned recapture merely changes which enemy minor falls and trades off Black’s bishop. The full-game position and actual move are valid, but the pin must change the stated gain to qualify.

After ...Kg7 Rxf6 Bf1, the bishop recovers two pawns and the tested line relies on a promotion to restore the gain. Other non-pin moves already keep a decisive engine advantage. The visible pawn gain is too transient for Beginner.

Ra3 stops f4 and wins a pawn within the local horizon, but the rook-versus-bishop position already has many straightforward winning moves including the played Ra7. In the strongest Kf4 Rxf3+ Kg5 line White also recovers g6 before the rook wins h4. A conversion with a temporary pawn gain does not isolate the Beginner pin lesson.

The pawn can be won without the pin. Removing Bc4 makes the e6 pawn recapture legal, but exf5 exf5 gxf5 still wins a clean pawn (+100 cp) with no subsequent Black capture. The played gxf5 has the same independent mechanism. Both White pawns attack f5, so a second capture supplies the entire stated gain even without the pinned defender.

Nxd4 genuinely uses the c6 pin: removing Bb5 permits ...Nxd4, and cxd4 Rxc1 loses the nominal gain. However the independent forcing Bxc6+ bxc6 cxd4 swaps bishop for knight and retains the same pawn without exploiting a restricted recapture. A targeted 1.5M-node probe found the strongest ...Ne7, followed by an ordinary quiet continuation with the pawn retained. Also checked the weaker one-move cxd4, which uses the same pin but gives Black active pressure and is not the bypass. Choose a clearer A case without the simple exchange-and-capture alternative.

The played Rxg7+ removes the pinned knight directly and wins more than the analysis Nxe6. There are three legal replies: after ...Kh8 White keeps the whole knight and can take a7; ...Kf8 or ...Kxg7 permits Nxe6+ followed by Nxd4, a direct king-rook fork. The alternative is a clearer forcing capture and defeats the intended one-move pawn lesson.

Rh4 pins and wins the knight, but the starting rook-versus-two-minors position already has many high-scoring quiet continuations because of the pawn majority. The h4-to-knight rank pin and pawn counterplay also repeat the published Bacrot example. Prefer clearer distinct Beginner decisions.

exf5 takes a knight with a pawn. If the e6-pawn could recapture, White still gains a knight for a pawn (+220 cp), the same nominal gain as the legal immediate reply ...dxc5. The pin does not enable the material gain.

dxe5 wins a knight for a pawn even if hypothetical ...fxe5 is allowed (+220 cp before any retake). The legal ...Rxe5 also permits immediate recovery, and Rxe5 itself is a competing capture. The pin is incidental to the immediate material objective.

The a4–d1 pin is real, but 54...Ba4 55.Kc1 Bxb3 56.Kb2 attacks both the knight a3 and bishop b3. Retreating the bishop (e.g. ...Bc2) allows Kxa3, and moving the knight with ...Nc4+ allows Kxb3. The stronger defensive sequence therefore recovers the entire extra knight. This also substantially repeats the published Black Bb5–a4 pin and Bxb3 decision, daa80783925e077c.
exclusions.distinctness: The occupied front square is a knight rather than a rook, but the same color, bishop start and destination, pin line, and capture repeat the existing learner decision. The new fork by the white king erases the putative gain rather than providing a distinct verified exercise.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Ba4 would be the unique root in the one-response local horizon. It prevents true knight escapes to a1, a5, c1 and d2, but the pin does not protect the gain against the later Kb2 fork.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 20 legal roots compared. Nc4 Nc1 and Bd7 h4 fail the short gain, even though Black maintains a large advantage. Starting material already favors Black by a bishop, so other moves giving a winning endgame are expected and are not unique pin solutions.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Seven legal immediate replies and the local Bxb3 witness rechecked. Deeper packet line Kc1 Bxb3 Kb2 Nc4+ Kxb3 erases the knight gain. Supplemental 500k-node probes show Kb2 Bc2 Kxa3 and Kb2 Kc4 Kxa3 also erase it. No legal capture of the bishop immediately after Ba4, but the subsequent double attack is decisive.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces, but fails the enduring introductory material payoff and substantially duplicates an approved exercise.
reviewNotes.provenance: Sorbe–Lai, Titled Tue 14th Jul, 2026-07-14. Exact TWIC 1654 replay through 54.Nb3 at ply 107, White FM in source. The game played 54...Kc4. Ba4 is an unplayed analytical candidate only.

exclusions.reason: Bxd5 is a genuine alternative to Rc5. Declining the bishop recapture preserves the full bishop gain. After Bxd5 Kxd5, the pawn b4 protects c5 and Rc5+ skewers the king and remaining bishop. All four legal king replies allow Rxg5, maintaining +330 cp after every immediate response. The independent three-move capture-and-skewer route makes the intended pin an unsuitable single-answer lesson.

Ra3 isolates the pawn tactically, but the rook-versus-bishop position already offers numerous more effective quiet moves. Rb4 Bd6 Rd4 and Ke3 Bb6+ both outscore Ra3 and can force later material. The same pawn-and-rook mechanism was already withheld in the earlier Olympiad source.

The h3-pawn gives Black a large advantage across many quiet roots, including Kg2 and Rf8. The nominal knight gain is real but a routine conversion is already available without it. The most prominent source threat is promotion rather than the pin.

The played Bxd4 already secures material through every legal immediate reply. Even the strongest recapture Bxd4 Rxd4+ leaves +100 cp, and every other reply admits an immediate material witness of at least +170. The alternative exchanges bishops directly, so the pin is not essential to gaining material.

Black can win a pawn immediately by the simple played Rxh3 without using the pin. The only White capture in reply is Rxg3+, which Black can answer with Kxg3 for a greater gain. The stronger Bf4 exchange does not make that direct bypass acceptable, especially with Black already a full bishop ahead.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Bf4 pins the rook and makes the larger gain possible, but the pin is unnecessary to gain material.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 22 legal roots compared. Rxh3 has a secure pawn gain, even if White captures the bishop with Rxg3+ and Black recaptures the rook. The local gate reports false because it stops immediately at the nominal loss after Rxg3+ before considering the winning recapture.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Bf4 does have a short gain against all four legal replies, including Bxg5 Kxg5 after Kg6 or Kh5. That does not resolve the independent pawn gain.
reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces but the direct pawn capture and initial full-bishop advantage undermine the intended decision.
reviewNotes.provenance: Schekachikhin–Liavonava, 1st 3-0 Thu 12th Mar 2026. Checksummed TWIC 1636 replays to exact ply 145 after Rg5. The actual move Rxh3 is the bypass.

exclusions.reason: Rc2 creates a real pin, but the original game has a simpler non-pin plan for the stated material goal. Black can trade knights first with 60...Nxd2 61.Kxd2, then ...Rh1. Exhaustive local replay after ...Rh1 shows all seven legal replies permit a safe capture of h3 or h4 on the next Black turn for +100 cp. This was also the game continuation after Ke3, and 1M-node comparison found several similarly favorable rook moves. The original knight exchange does not need the pin and retains Black’s already large material edge.
exclusions.distinctness: Pinning instead keeps the black knight and wins the entire defender, but a larger payoff does not cure the straightforward material bypass. The full TWIC 1643 replay confirms 60...Nxd2 and Black’s later ...Rxh3+.

exclusions.reason: The exact two-solver-turn gate misses two genuine three-turn alternatives. After either Rd7 or Rb5, a complete short material tree covers all 19 legal first replies and all next defences, with net material retained through the immediate reply. The rook wins Bb7 if it stays, while Bf3 Rh7 or Bf3 Rb4 leaves Black able to win a minor piece on the next turn. Rh5 is not a unique sound material move.

Ra1 really pins Ba4, and all six legal first replies allow Rxa4. But 1...Ra1 2.Kb7 Rxa4 3.d7 forces a stronger pawn defence: ...Rd4 4.Kc7 ...Kf6 5.d8=Q+ Rxd8 6.Kxd8 erases the bishop gain and leaves −70 cp incremental material. A 1M-node comparison also found ...Rb4+ leads to the same rook surrender, while ...Ra2 and ...Re4 permit a decisive promotion. The remaining g-pawn gives Black the favourable engine result, which is a separate endgame objective.
exclusions.distinctness: A real file pin with a nearby outside passer, but the passer changes the decision from a short material win to a promotion race. Original composition, with no game or preceding move.

exclusions.reason: Bxb7 is a genuine alternative to Rb5. After Bxb7 Kxb7, Rb5+ checks the king and attacks the remaining bishop on b4. All six legal king replies permit Rxb4 and a durable +330 cp through every immediate reply. Declining the recapture leaves White an initial bishop gain, and the strongest tested Nd4 line also retains material. This capture-and-double-attack route defeats the single-answer pin lesson.

Re3 pins Ne4 and gives a local knight gain, but White starts with a rook and outside passer against a lone knight. The pin is unnecessary to resolve the contest in a clear practical win, and the played h5 Kd7 h6 Nd6 h7 develops a more immediate decision than the pin. All 20 legal roots reviewed. Supplementary 1M-node comparisons for h5 and Ra7+ give several strong material-winning conversion routes based on the passer. Published exercises already cover quiet rook moves that pin and collect a knight.
exclusions.distinctness: An uncomplicated file pin, but it asks the learner to collect a knight in an already dominant position rather than to find a pin needed for the immediate contest. The correct exact source game shows h5, so Re3 would be an analysis line only.

exclusions.reason: Nxc4 offers a direct alternative to the analysis Rc8. If Black recaptures with Kxc4, the targeted line Ke3 Kd5 Rxb3 wins the advanced pawn and retains +110 cp. If Black plays b2, Rxb2 Kxc4 likewise leaves +110 cp, and declining the exchange can leave a whole bishop gain. Deeper screening ranks Nxc4 higher than Rc8. The original position already has a substantial material edge, and the pin is unsuitable as its unique short material lesson.

Qxa3 is an independent direct capture of a passed pawn, with a short material gain on every immediate reply. Black’s only reply that reduces the initial nominal gain is Qxb3, which permits Qxb3 or Rxb3, gaining the queen for a bishop and leaving +670 cp. The root comparison puts the pawn capture near the Bxe6 analysis, and supplemental 1M-node analysis after Qxa3 Bd4 confirms White can retain the gain in a sound continuation. The pin is real but unnecessary for the same stated pawn gain.
exclusions.distinctness: Two versions of the pin capture, the played Rxe6 and the unplayed Bxe6, both compete with the unrelated direct Qxa3. Neither is a suitable A exercise under the essential-motif rule.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Without the a7 queen, Black’s fxe6 becomes legal and changes the Bxe6 pawn gain from +100 cp to −230 cp. White can take on e6 or a3 once more, but either capture still leaves −130 cp. The actual pin is essential to Bxe6 specifically.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 38 legal starts compared. Qxa3 alone wins the passed pawn on a3, with Qxb3 immediately losing the queen to two legal recaptures. Rxe6 was played and uses the same pin. No positive mate score.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: No immediate legal capture of either participant after Bxe6. All 41 first replies leave +100 cp. The strong ...Qb1+ Kh2 ...Qd1 allows counterplay against c2 or d6. In 1M-node replays, White can recover or preserve the nominal advantage through exact play, but these lines do not invalidate the simpler Qxa3 bypass.
reviewNotes.level: Direct pin capture in isolation, but rejected at A because the same short objective can already be obtained without the pin.
reviewNotes.provenance: Xiong–Bortnyk, Titled Tue, 2025-11-20. Both GM in TWIC 1620 archived headers. Exact FEN follows 44...Bf6 at source ply 88 and the game played 45.Rxe6. Bxe6 is an unplayed analysis candidate. Archive checksum retained.

exclusions.reason: Qxd4 is sound, but Bxc6+ provides a nearly equivalent direct forcing route and removes the need to exploit the blocked recapture. All three replies were checked in the exact local tree. After bxc6, Qxd4 retains a pawn after the equivalent bishop-for-knight trade. Ke7 permits Bxb7 and Qd7 permits Bxd7+. A separate Ne2 route also achieves a comparable short result. The played position is too ambiguous as a direct pawn lesson.
exclusions.distinctness: The played Qxd4 differs from Lodici–Prakhar Tripathi by the bishop pin on the knight, but the check-and-exchange alternative dominates the editorial decision.

exclusions.reason: The pin is real, but the adjacent checking capture Rxf7+ followed by Rxe5 already wins material in every legal defence. Kxf7 Rxe5 trades rooks and wins the knight, and the three other king replies also allow Rxe5 with durable gain. Stockfish evaluates the alternative nearly as highly, and it is a simple competing order of forcing captures for this material lesson.

The immediate pawn capture is legal and pin-dependent, but the strongest reply Ng6+ forks the king and rook. After Kf6 Nxh8, the targeted line needs Nxc3 bxc3 Bxc3+ Ke2 Bxa1 Rxa1 Rxh8 to recover material. The short pawn win is therefore a poor Level A lesson, and the published Akobian–Boyer Nxe4 already teaches a simpler bishop pin on a knight enabling this exact pawn capture.
exclusions.distinctness: Published 4928a7e02ac06872 uses the same blocked knight recapture and same Nxe4 decision. The new white knight fork adds calculation beyond Level A.

exclusions.reason: The simpler alternative Nxf4 wins a pawn without needing the pinned bishop’s blocked recapture. After the strongest Rxf4, Black immediately takes the exposed bishop with Rxe1+, an equal knight-for-bishop exchange that keeps +110 cp. The 850k-node reply search confirms this and the leading Kf1 or Kh2 alternatives also retain the pawn.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Without Rb1 the intended Nxc3 permits Bxc3, losing a knight for a pawn (-220 cp). The pin is necessary for this exact capture but another direct material win is available.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 23 roots compared, with no mate in one or forced mate in two. Nxf4 Rxf4 Rxe1+ is the direct alternative, and the b1 rook can capture the bishop whether or not it was pinned. No extra preparation is needed.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 14 replies to Nxc3 keep the pawn and neither the knight nor rook is offered. Re3 Nd5 retains the gain. The independent Nxf4 Rxf4 Rxe1+ also retains the gain under practical resistance, so the advertised decision is compromised.
reviewNotes.level: The named tactic is direct, but a competing direct material win makes the position unsuitable.
reviewNotes.provenance: Askarov–Theodorou, Titled Tue 17th Feb 2026, checksummed TWIC 1633. Exact ply 95 after Rxe4. Nxc3 was played.

exclusions.reason: Capturing the pinned bishop with check already wins material by the simple alternative Rxg2+ Rxg2 Rxd5, giving +330 cp. Against the only other legal answers Kh1 or Kh3, Rxd5 wins even more. This bypasses the stated need to use the pin for the rook capture.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Without Rf2, Bxd5+ is legal after Rxd5 and erases the gain. The pin matters to the immediate line but is unnecessary to win material from the start.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 24 legal roots compared and exact legal replay excludes mate in one or forced mate in two. Rxg2+ has exactly three replies. Against Rxg2, Rxd5 wins +330 cp and survives four high-ranked 850k continuations. Against Kh1 or Kh3, Rxd5 also wins immediately.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 12 replies to Rxd5 retain at least +400 cp. Rxg6+ can be met by hxg6. Neither the pinner nor capturing rook is immediately offered. This does not rule out the simple independent gain.
reviewNotes.level: Two clear material-winning decisions make this a weak fit for a direct pinned-defender exercise.
reviewNotes.provenance: Weetik–Tabatabaei, Titled Tue 24th Feb 2026, checksummed TWIC 1634. Exact ply 73 after White Rxd5. The game played Black Rxd5.

deferred.reason: The g2 pawn genuinely cannot recapture (hypothetical ...gxf3 turns +100 cp into −230 cp and ...Nxd4 Rxd4 cannot rescue it). However the exact Rb1, Ra1 and Re5 defence probes show material recovery on the queenside. The original Rb1 line drops the full pawn after Rxb7, ...Nxd4 and Rxa7. Targeted 1M-node MultiPV finds Rb1 ...Rg7 Rb4 ...Be4 Rdb2 ...Rg8, but keeping the increment through the rook activity relies on additional precise play. Hold for a fuller direct material witness before presenting it as A.
Bd5–Rxe6 geometry and exchange against Kf7 replicate the same decision as the selected Vazelakis position. Prefer the more distinct black-to-move Sokolov–Ivanchuk recovery example for this family.
deferred.distinctness: A bishop pins a rook, with the unusual defence of letting its king recapture on the pinned square. The learner must distinguish winning the whole rook from winning the exchange.
deferred.solutionVi: Bd5 — Tượng trắng từ e4 đến d5, ghim Xe e6 vào Vua g8. Nếu Đen chơi Kf7, Trắng bắt Xe bằng Bxe6+. Đen có thể đáp Kxe6, nhưng Trắng vẫn lời vì đổi Tượng lấy Xe.
hintsVi: Tìm đường chéo đi qua Xe e6 và Vua g8.
Nếu Vua đen tiến tới f7, hãy so sánh giá trị của Xe và Tượng.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Bd5 pins the rook and prevents actual escapes such as ...Rf6, seen after the quiet alternative Kf1. Off-line rook moves would expose K g8.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: 17 legal roots, one positive outcome. Kf1 Rf6 and Bd3 Rb6 let the rook escape, while Bh7+ Kxh7 loses the bishop. No immediate mate.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All six replies allow Bxe6. Kf7 Bxe6+ Kxe6 is the only immediate recapture and retains +170 cp. The deep ...Kf7 line also confirms the exchange, and five other replies allow a full rook capture. No capture of the bishop is possible before the payoff.
reviewNotes.level: 9 pieces and one bishop move. The one short recapture still makes a straightforward exchange gain.
reviewNotes.provenance: Vachier Lagrave–Carlsen, Opera Euro Rapid KO 2021, checksummed PGN Mentor records. Exact ply 76 and preceding Rxe6 verified. Bd5 was played.

deferred.reason: Rank pin of a bishop from a rook is covered by the cleaner black-to-move Ra4 and by Ra6 where the rook itself escapes attack. The extra pawn recovery here dilutes the contrast.
deferred.distinctness: Black’s rook pins the bishop across the fifth rank against a king that can approach and take g7. This version illustrates taking the major gain despite the smaller pawn recovery. Similar rank geometry to Ra4 in this packet, so select according to coverage.
deferred.solutionVi: Rb5 — Xe từ b4 đến b5, ghim Tượng d5 vào Vua g5. Sau Kg6, Đen bắt Tượng bằng Rxd5. Nếu Trắng bắt tốt g7 bằng Kxg7, Đen vẫn lời một Tượng đổi lấy một tốt.
hintsVi: Tìm hàng ngang đi qua cả Tượng d5 và Vua g5.
Xe Đen có thể đi đến đâu để giữ Tượng d5 trên hàng đó?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rb5 creates the absolute rank pin. The bishop cannot escape to squares such as e6 or f7, cannot capture Rb5, and cannot be saved by any of the five king moves.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: One answer in the 21-root short-payoff proof. Rxg4+ Kxg4 loses the rook. After Kd8 Kg6 Rxg4+ the pawn capture depends on the king voluntarily leaving g4 and is not forced. Rd4 Ba2 lets the bishop escape. No mate bypass.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Every White reply is a king move and permits Rxd5 or Rxd5+. After the strongest Kg6 Rxd5 Kxg7, the net gain remains 230 cp. The moved rook cannot be captured after Rb5 or on d5 in the verified line.
reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces, one quiet rook move, no offer. The capture is clear on the next turn even if White gets a pawn back.
reviewNotes.provenance: Uber Gracia–Fernandez Ramos, 2026-06-18, TWIC 1650. Full checksum-bound game at ply 85 after Kg5; Rb5 Kg6 Rxd5 was played.

deferred.reason: Rf7 is a valid unique short pin, but White starts up a rook against a knight with an extra pawn and several ordinary continuations already score well over +5. Rf6 or Rh8 often harvests a pawn later. The similar balanced Rf1 position gives the same direct pin decision with a more meaningful threat from the pinned knight.

Bd5 to pin e6 against Kg8 repeats the decision and king-recapture geometry of the stronger black-to-move Vazelakis example. The selected source also avoids the long kingside pawn race in this game’s Kf7 continuation.

Rc4 wins a bishop, but b6 Bxb6 Rxb6 already yields a durable net +230, and targeted deeper alternatives to ...Bxb6 repeatedly allow promotion. The exact short proof rejects b6 because the alternatives can take more turns, so it does not settle whether the material goal has a second sound answer. Defer for the single-answer format.

Rc4 uniquely wins the knight within the local horizon, but the rook-versus-knight starting advantage already gives several high-scoring routine lines. For example, Rc1 Nd6 Rxc5 and Re2 Ng3 Rc2 Nh5 Rxc5 gain a pawn; choose a position where the pin changes the contest more clearly.

Verified reserve. Smietanska–Janaszak already teaches the bishop capture of one of two mutually defending knights while the rook’s own capture loses the exchange. That example has the additional counterattack Bb6 against the pinning rook.
deferred.distinctness: Two enemy knights defend each other but one is pinned on the back rank. The learner chooses the distant knight with a bishop while keeping the rook in place. Capturing the pinned knight with the rook instead loses the exchange.
deferred.solutionVi: Phương án phân tích. Bxd6 — Tượng từ f4 bắt Mã d6. Xe h8 ghim Mã e8 vào Vua d8, nên Mã e8 không thể bắt lại ở d6.
hintsVi: Hai Mã Đen ở d6 và e8 đang bảo vệ nhau. Mã nào bị Xe ghim vào Vua?
Xét nước bắt Mã d6 bằng Tượng và kiểm tra xem Đen có thể bắt lại hay không.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rh8 pins Ne8 to Kd8 on the eighth rank. Removing Rh8 as a geometric counterfactual permits ...Nxd6, leaving White 10 cp below the adjusted starting balance with no legal retake on d6. On the actual board ...Nxd6 would expose the king.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 37 legal roots compared and no immediate mate. Rxe8+ Nxe8 loses the exchange; the strongest quiet alternatives Bg4 and Bg6 leave Black the knight pair and yield no comparable material gain.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 16 legal replies are non-captures, so neither the moving bishop nor Rh8 is offered. The strongest ...Rg7 line keeps the knight gain and White can answer the eventual ...Rxg4 with Kxg4; the forcing ...Re2+ is met by Kxe2. No immediate recapture can recover the knight.
reviewNotes.level: One direct capture, no preparation and no material offer. The two knights and their reciprocal defence make the pin immediately visible.
reviewNotes.provenance: Ibadov–Mayaud, 1st 3-0 Thu 24th Sep 2026, checksum-bound TWIC 1664. The full game matches ply 80 after ...Kd8. White played Bg6; Bxd6 is analysis.

deferred.reason: The unique short-horizon pin is genuine, but the strongest defence recovers White’s g5 pawn and the settled pawn gain is too long for Beginner. Rc7 Nh3 Rxf7+ Kg8 (or Rc7 Kg8 Rxf7 Nh3) requires Rf3 Nxg5 Rg3 Ne4 Rxg6+ in the supplemented million-node review. The simpler Rf6 meets Kg7 and transposes back after Rf7+ Kg8. Re7, Ke7 or Rf1 simply allow Nxg5. The result should be reconsidered for an appropriate later grade with a complete line.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rc7 newly pins f7 to Kg7, forbidding f7-f5 and giving a safe immediate capture after every legal reply. This passes the short local pin proof.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 13 legal roots compared. Rc5 Ne6 and Ra8 Ne6 do not force material, and several rook retreats allow Ne6 and Nxg5. Rc7 is the only root passing the local one-move proof. No immediate mate or competing capture.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All ten immediate replies allow Rxf7 or Kxf7. No capture of the rook on c7 is possible. Strong Nh3 and Kg8 transpose and temporarily recover the pawn on g5. The earliest strong supplementary gain after recovery is on the fifth solver move, after a rook chase from f3 to g3.
reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces and one required root, but the strongest defensive resource obscures the durable payoff. Hold for a grade that can show the full line.
reviewNotes.provenance: Kamsky–Guseinov, FIDE World Blitz 2013, checksummed PGN Mentor Kamsky game. Full game replays to exact ply 128 after Nf4. Rc7 was played, followed by Ne6 in the drawn game.

deferred.reason: The played 10.Bxe5 is a sound reserve candidate. All 36 roots and 23 immediate replies were checked. Without the d1 rook, ...Nxe5 is legal, changes +100 cp to −230 cp, and leaves no White capture. ...c6 Nf3 and 1.5M-node spot checks against ...Nh6, ...f6 and ...Nf6 support a lasting pawn gain, with no material offer needed. This packet selects a different defence mechanism for the single available slot. A published A exercise already uses a rook to pin a knight for a bishop capture, and this position has a smaller teaching payoff.
deferred.distinctness: The attacked bishop f4 captures its attacking pawn and relies on the file pin of Nd7. Published 15927fbe436bc2e2 also uses a rook pin on a knight for a bishop capture, but takes a knight rather than a pawn.

deferred.reason: The source and payoff check out, but the learner decision repeats the already published Schmidt–Strehse Rxf6. Both use a white rook on the f-file to take a bishop on f6, while a stationary white rook on the g-file pins g7 to Kg8; both face counterplay from two black rooks, including a rook check on the d-file and possible pawn recovery. Reserve it for future selection and prefer a different A decision.
deferred.distinctness: Matches published f203d080397d92fc in capturing piece, target, destination, pinned defender, king square, and practical reply family. Starting rook ranks and the exact black check differ.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rg4 pins g7 to Kg8. Removing the pinner as a counterfactual permits ...gxf6, yielding −170 cp relative to the adjusted start with no White retake.

deferred.reason: Rf6 is a valid one-move pin and wins the knight. The learner decision and the practical defence are too close to published Eynullayev–Bacrot Rh4. Each uses the rook alone to pin and win an otherwise mobile knight across a rank; the opposing king cannot protect the knight, but an advanced outside passer can move instead of the king and the rook can contain it after the capture. This is also routine conversion from an existing +280 cp material edge, with several quiet moves preserving a large advantage. Keep as a reserve rather than repeat the lesson.
deferred.distinctness: Compared with 6c3148b00cd1c6f4 Rh4, White has its own potential passed f-pawn and the knight starts adjacent to the rook destination, but the choices of how to create the pin and how the opponent responds are materially the same.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rf6 pins Ne6 to Ka6 across the sixth rank. Knight moves such as Nc7 or Nd4 would escape the rook attack but expose the king. A direct vertical attack Re5 allows Nd8 and does not guarantee the capture.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 13 roots reviewed and no immediate mate. Rxb5 Kxb5 loses a rook for a pawn, while Rd5 Nc7 and Re5 Nd8 let the knight escape. There is one solution for the exact short horizon; the other quiet roots retain a large pre-existing positional advantage without winning the knight immediately.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: No legal capture of Rf6 after the pin. All five responses admit Rxe6 or Rxe6+ with +320 cp through the immediate reply. The Kb7 and Ka5 lines control the b-pawn and preserve the gain. The Kb6 branch can trade the rook only after the f-pawn promotes; material remains above the initial balance.
reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces, one quiet rook move, immediate knight payoff in the review horizon and no material offer. Editorial hold reflects collection overlap rather than the level or legality.
reviewNotes.provenance: Morozevich–Piesik, Titled Arena May 8th 2021, checksum-bound PGN Mentor Morozevich archive. Full replay reaches ply 112 after ...b5. The game played Re5 b4 Rxe6+; Rf6 is analysis.

deferred.reason: The bishop pins a rook on the same short diagonal and permits the same king recapture as the earlier Bd5 examples. Against Kd7 Bxd6 Kxd6, the best continuation temporarily gives up g5 and b6 and depends on a queenside promotion race. A cleaner new Beginner decision is preferable.

The all-root comparison also favors Rxf5. The reply ...gxf5 stops a short gain but the deeper position still contains a playable tactic, while the strongest ...g5 line returns to Be3. This leaves a complicated competing decision for Beginner and repeats the bishop-rook capture motif.

Ba2 genuinely traps the knight and stops the a-pawn at the short horizon, but c7 supplies a competing forcing material tactic without the pin. Supplemental 800k-node reply comparisons find the strongest c7 Bxc7 Rxc7+ Kf6 Ra7 Nd2 Rxa3 retains +330 cp material. Against Ke7 the straightforward promotion idea continues Re8+ Kxe8 c8=Q+. Even though other replies require a rook offer or calculation, the advanced pawn makes the named material decision less clear for this collection.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Ba2 creates a2–b3–f7 pin on the knight and also physically stops the a3 pawn. The knight could otherwise escape via Nd4 or Na5.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 21 legal roots were compared. c7 is not a one-move finite proof, yet it gives an independent promotion tactic or gain by recapture against the most relevant replies. Rh8 allows Bxh8 and does not give a clean pawn gain. No immediate mate.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 18 legal replies to Ba2 permit Bxb3 or Bxb3+ and hold +320 cp through the next legal reply. No immediate capture of the bishop is possible. The supplementary Bc3 Bxb3+ probe also retains a gain.
reviewNotes.level: The pin line alone suits Beginner, but the natural winning pawn thrust competes for the same broad objective and puts advanced promotion calculation on the board.
reviewNotes.provenance: Southcott-Moyers–Shanmathi Sree, Titled Tue 17th Feb 2026. Checksummed TWIC 1633 replays to exact ply 116 after Be5. Ba2 and Ke7 Bxb3 were played.

deferred.reason: Sound reserve. Bulmaga–Schulze teaches the same five-piece exchange into king and pawn versus king, and its complete game records the king recapture as well.
deferred.distinctness: Compare Martinez Alcantara–Bok Bd3, where the pin defends an h-pawn under attack and several pawns remain after the exchange. This five-piece source isolates the choice to trade into king and pawn versus king, with no opposing pawns or further material calculation.
deferred.solutionVi: Bf5 — Tượng từ d3 đến f5, ghim Xe e6 vào Vua d7. Sau Kd6, Trắng bắt Xe bằng Bxe6. Nếu Đen đáp Kxe6, Trắng đã đổi Tượng lấy Xe và còn tốt c2.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Bf5 aligns the bishop, rook and king on f5–e6–d7. The rook could otherwise escape to e7 or f6 and cannot travel along the pin line.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 14 roots examined. Bb5+ Kd6 Bc4 Re8 lets the rook get away, and there is no initial capture or immediate mate. Only Bf5 has the verified short material gain.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The new bishop is not offered to any legal capture. All seven replies are king moves and allow Bxe6 or Bxe6+. Kd6 and Ke7 allow Kxe6 after the capture, but both leave White a pawn against the bare king with a net exchange gain of 170 cp. The deeper Kc3 lines retain the pawn.
reviewNotes.level: Five pieces, one quiet bishop move and a visible exchange. No pawn-ending calculation is needed to understand the material objective.
reviewNotes.provenance: Haug–Tari, 3rd 3-0 Thu 9th Apr 2026, checksum-bound TWIC 1640. Full game replays to ply 146 after ...Kxd7. Bf5 Kd6 Bxe6 is the played line; the possible Kxe6 is a continuation beyond the recorded game.

deferred.reason: Valid reserve with a uniquely forced, durable bishop win. All 19 legal roots and eight first replies checked. Rb4 wins Bd4 on every reply, including the strongest king advance Kf4 Rxd4+, while the played Rd7 allows Bb6. The already published White Rb6 in Shirov–Topalov and Rb7 in Shuvalova–Zhu both move up or down the b-file to pin a bishop on the d-file along a rank and collect it with the same rook. This position has no comparably different learner choice or defensive mechanism.
deferred.distinctness: All three start with a white rook on the b-file, put it on the bishop’s rank, and use Rxd-file capture. The different king and pawn squares do not change the decisive action. The candidate root Rb4 was not played; the exact TWIC 1657 game finished with Rd7 from the supplied FEN.

deferred.reason: Ra6 is a genuine analysis pin and wins a knight across all eight replies. The same rook-only rank pin against an unguarded knight already appears in Eynullayev–Bacrot Rh4 and the near-equivalent 08c2bda827327149 Rf6 was held. This position also starts +280 cp materially and many quiet moves hold a large edge, so the added knight mainly accelerates an already favorable conversion.
deferred.distinctness: Compare 6c3148b00cd1c6f4 Rh4 and deferred 08c2bda827327149 Rf6. The pins trap a mobile knight with the same forced capture, while the opposing king is too far away to save it. The f- and h-pawn pushes and longer rank distance here add variation without changing the main decision.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Ra6 creates the a6–d6–g6 pin and prevents real escapes such as Ne4 and Nf7. The rook itself takes on d6 next.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Reviewed all 23 roots, including Rg4+ hxg4 and quiet moves. Actual Rf4 allows Nf7 or Ne4 and gives no quick material gain. Ra6 alone passes the exact short payoff test.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All eight replies admit Rxd6 or Rxd6+. No legal capture of the rook after Ra6. Kf6 Rxd6+ settles the gain and ...f4 Rxd6+ likewise captures with tempo. The deeper ...f4 line can also collect the pawn before taking the knight and retains the knight gain.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces and one non-sacrificial rook move. Editorial hold for redundancy and a large existing advantage.
reviewNotes.provenance: Murawski–Salemgareev, Titled Tue 21st Apr 2026, complete and checksum-bound TWIC 1642 game. Exact ply 94 after ...f5. Ra6 is analysis; Rf4 was played.

deferred.reason: Qe3 immediately attacks both Be5 and Nh6 and is favored by the full all-root comparison. Its strongest Kg6 Qxe5 already wins a bishop. The competing queen fork obscures the beginner pin decision.
Sound reserve. The scoped selection prefers a complete-game example or a more distinct learner decision in this teaching family.
deferred.distinctness: Black places the bishop on rank one and pins along the long c1–h6 diagonal. It captures the knight itself and can do so with check when White tries to push a distant pawn. This differs from the shorter published Bg5 pin, where the solver’s king can also take the knight, and the Bf4 and Be4 examples that pin rooks.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: After Bc1, the c1–h6 diagonal bars real knight escapes such as Nc4 and Ne4. Without the pin these moves leave the bishop’s line. Bc1 is a quiet move that attacks and restrains Nd2.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 18 legal starts checked. Be7 allows Nc4, Bb4 allows Ne4, Kf7 allows Ne4 and Bf8+ allows Kg6. None forces a short material gain or mating shortcut.

Supplementary 1M-node probes after both b4 Bxd2+ and f6 Bxd2+ confirmed continuations that hold the knight gain and take one of the passed pawns.
reviewNotes.level: Beginner. Seven pieces, one quiet pin, clear knight capture, no offer. The two passed pawns provide contest without a complicated defensive refutation.
reviewNotes.provenance: Original composition pin-composed-5db5c2b1eaa5654a. Exact FEN and move checked. No real game, event, player attribution, or preceding move.

deferred.reason: Sound reserve. The scoped selection prefers a complete-game example or a more distinct learner decision in this teaching family.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Bg4 pins the white rook along g4–f5–e6–d7–c8. Otherwise Re7 or Rc6 can move the rook out of the attack.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Compared all 28 legal roots. h5 allows Kc7 Bg4 Rc6, and Rc5+ permits Kb8, without winning material. No immediate capture or mate bypass.

reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces. A single quiet pin is the unique short material-gaining answer. The knight counterattack is answered by the same obvious capture.
reviewNotes.provenance: Original composition, exact FEN and canonical composition ID. No source game or preceding move.

deferred.reason: Rh4 is the only root that wins promptly through every reply in the finite proof, but Rcc3 creates a competing doubled-rook tactic against the second knight. Against the strongest Kb4 and several relevant knight replies, Rxa3 or Rxa3+ wins the same piece without Rh4. In some other replies Rcc3 permits immediate mate. The strongest lines without the second capture ultimately return to the pin, but the competing first decision makes the position less clear for Beginner.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rh4 genuinely pins Ng4 to Ka4 and deprives the knight of real escapes such as Ne5 and Nf2.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 29 roots and no immediate mate. Rcc3 Kb4 Rxa3 retains +320 cp in a supplemental 800k-node probe. After Rcc3 Ne5 the same Rxa3+ also keeps the knight. Rcc3 Nb5 permits Rc4#, and after Bd6 the stronger continuation returns to the pin with Rh4 rather than a quick capture.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 13 replies to Rh4 permit Rxg4 for +320 cp with no rook offered. The strongest Kb3 and Be5 lines confirm that gain. This verifies the pin itself, while the doubled-rook alternative remains a competing teaching decision.
reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces but two independent near-term threats and 29 legal moves. Defer in favor of a clear unique instructional decision.
reviewNotes.provenance: Original composition, exact legal starting FEN. No source game or preceding move.

deferred.reason: Rh2 uniquely traps Ng2 in the bounded proof, but many quiet rook moves already score above +350. The rank pin with a distant king and checking capture also repeats an already published family.

deferred.solutionVi: Thế cờ biên soạn. Ra2 — Xe trắng từ a7 đến a2, ghim Tượng c2 vào Vua f2. Nếu Đen chen Tượng còn lại vào d2 bằng Bd2, Trắng vẫn bắt Tượng ở c2 bằng Rxc2.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Ra2 creates the a2–c2–f2 rank pin, preventing escapes such as Bb3+. The other bishop can interpose at d2, but White moves next and the target stays on c2.

Against Bb8 Rxc2+ Ke3 the supplementary 800k-node Rc8 and Rc6 lines preserve +330 cp without offering the rook. The Rc7 choice instead deliberately trades the rook to create a winning passer, outside the proof needed for the lesson.

Sound reserve. The scoped selection prefers a complete-game example or a more distinct learner decision in this teaching family.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rf5 leaves the attacked f3 square and creates the f5–d5–a5 rank pin. Without it the bishop can escape off the rank, as with Be6+ after Rd3.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 17 roots compared. a2 Bxa2 loses the pawn. Kxh2 permits Bxf3, leaving Black down a rook before attempting counterpromotion. The supplemental 800k-node analysis also finds Nb5 Rf5 Nxa3 restores material balance after Kxh2. The quiet Rf8 alternative allows Kb4 and no immediate gain. No mate.

The supplied Kb4 line and supplemented Ka4 branch agree that Ra5+ Kb4 Rxa7 extends the gain; it is unnecessary for the short objective. The rook is safe immediately after the root.

deferred.reason: The short diagonal Bd5–e6 and adjacent king recapture repeat the previously reviewed Bd5 exchange examples. The deeper Ke7 Bxe6 Kxe6 line loses a pawn and relies on the g-pawn race, which makes this less distinct for Beginner.

The immediate exchange gain is real, but the strongest Ke5 Bxe4 Kxe4 line allows ...Kxb3 and the sustained advantage depends on the distant h-pawn. The nearby king’s recapture after Bd3 repeats the previously approved Martinez Alcantara–Bok exercise.

Qh8 verifies a clean rook gain, but repeats the same corner-to-corner queen pin and prevention of repeated rook checks as the stronger balanced Bortnyk–Erigaisi Qa8 example. Here Black starts +300 cp, and Qh4, Qh7 and Qh3 already produce +342 to +386 cp with ordinary moves. Keep the more meaningful tactical contest.

deferred.reason: Bf7 does create the pin and the one-reply proof allows Bxe6+, but after the strongest Kd5 and the immediate Bxe6+ Kxe6, the two live promotion threats are decisive for evaluation. A 1M-node probe found g5 Kf7 g4 e6 g3 e7 g2 with both sides queening and equal assessment. The materially winning but practically clearest line after Kd5 requires an additional pawn advance before taking. The played h5 before the capture produced a draw. Reserve for a lesson on move order and promotion races rather than this short introductory collection.

In both positions, the bishop pins a knight guarded by the opposing king, while the friendly king sits adjacent and can also take after some king moves. The locked h-pawns here simplify the picture without changing the decision or recovery.

The benefit of this unplayed pin is entangled with the faster a-pawn lesson.

deferred.reason: Ba5 wins the rook cleanly, but repeats the published Giordani–Rosen Be7 decision. In each, the rook attacks the bishop, the bishop sidesteps to pin that same rook to its king, and no defensive reply can recover the rook. The defending white bishop adds reply count here without changing the outcome or the key decision.

deferred.reason: Rb3 passes the direct pin proof, but it is another rook-on-bishop rank pin in a position already +270 cp, with many ordinary moves at +340 to +435 cp and little counterplay before the pin. reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All seven legal replies allow Rxd3 or Rxd3+, preserving at least +230 cp immediately. No capture of the rook exists after Rb3. reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces and a clear local win, but the initial advantage and repeated mechanism make it a weaker introductory example.
reviewNotes.provenance: Barria Zuniga–Perez Gormaz, 3rd 3-0 Thu 4th Dec 2025, checksummed TWIC 1622. Exact ply 117 after Bd3. The actual move Kg6 is separate from the Rb3 analysis.

deferred.reason: The immediate gain is a pawn, but g4 h5 gxh5 returns it in the strongest tested line. The later knight win needs additional kingside calculation. The earlier Sjugirov–Aliyev exercise already teaches fxg5 against a pinned knight on f3.

The direct pawn capture is motif-dependent, but the practical gain after Ke5 is too sensitive for A. The played Rxd4 Kxd4 Kxe6 temporarily reduces the incremental gain to +20 cp and depends on a long promotion race. The strongest non-sacrificial alternative in a 1.2M-node probe, Re1+, allows Kxf5 immediately, erasing the pawn gain. The other active alternative f4 also permits Kxf4, and the basic king moves permit Nxf5. Reserve for a harder study on conversion after the pin is released.
deferred.distinctness: The initial rook pin prevents a checking knight recapture on f5. Its value is closely tied to whether the f-pawn can advance after White releases the pin, unlike the direct stationary pin and immediately secure exchange in the keep.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Removing the d1 rook permits Nxf5+, reducing the direct gain from +100 to zero with no immediate capture. The pin is needed for the first pawn gain.

reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All five replies preserve +100 cp immediately and neither participant can be captured. Exact supplemental 1M and 1.2M-node probes recorded.

The pin prevents immediate recapture, but Black can play ...f5 along the pin line. In the deeper direct g4 f4 Kg2 Ke7 Kf3 Kxe6 line Black recovers the only won pawn. The played Rd1 Ke7 Rd7+ Kxe6 Rxh7 restores a nominal pawn, but stronger play leaves recovery unresolved and the exact Kxe6 branch with Rxh7 is evaluated as level. The one-move material claim needs stronger settlement than this packet establishes.
deferred.distinctness: A pawn would take through a rook pin on the f-file. Unlike published Rosen–Mendonca Rxg4, the pinned pawn here can use a forward two-square advance to activate the king’s recovery.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rf1 pins Pf7 to Kf8 after fxe6. Removing it permits ...fxe6, bringing the gain to zero with no immediate White retake.

A retained material gain against the practical defence is unresolved.

deferred.reason: Rxe5 is motif-dependent and wins the pawn initially, but White cannot show a short durable material gain against active rook checks and attacks on both wings. The deep line Kh7 Re6 Rf7 Rbxd6 Rc3 Re3 Rc2+ Kd3 Rxh2 Kd4 Ra2 Ke5 Rxa5 returns both pawns. Reserve for a longer conversion study.

The distinctive extra challenge is the opposing pair of active rooks, which creates the unresolved short material recovery rather than a straightforward A variation.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Removing the b6 rook permits dxe5, changes the +100 cp gain to −400 cp, and leaves no legal White capture. The pin is necessary to take on e5 safely.

Stockfish remains favourable for White but the near-term gain is not durably established.

deferred.distinctness: Gyenes–Shirov Rxf4 uses a vertical rook pin of a bishop and saves the rook under attack. Here the pin is along the second rank, and the opponent can try Rb3 to attack the stationary pinner. The capturing rook supplies Rf4+ to keep the extra pawn through the trade.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rb2 pins Be2 to Kf2 along rank two. Removing Rb2 in the counterfactual permits Bxc4, which loses 400 cp relative to the adjusted start with no immediate Black retake.

deferred.reason: Bxf3+ Qxf3 Qxe5 wins the same bishop via the reverse order in the principal alternate line and retains +220 incremental material in the tactical probe. The choice is less clean than other direct A positions.

In addition, strong Rh1, a3 and b4 lines repeatedly recover the initial pawn by capturing a6. Supplemental 1M-node analysis finds a material-preserving plan after Rh1 and a3, but the main b4 line still returns the pawn and compensation relies on further double-rook play.
deferred.distinctness: One rook captures the pawn one file beside it, while the other rook on rank eight pins the defending pawn against a king on rank two. Published 67b810f4ffd0b2c9 already demonstrates this arrangement one file over. Here the technical rook counterplay is the main difference.

At 1M nodes, Rh1 Kf6 and a3 d5 have clear material-preserving routes, while b4 d5 Ra3 Rfg4 still allows later Rxa6. The stronger positional evaluation is not sufficient to resolve the short payoff.

Both have a stationary rook on b3 pinning a pawn along rank three and a bishop taking the pawn that it guards. The Be2 alternative also leads to a clear pawn win using the same rook and bishop support. Reserve in favour of examples from a more contested start and a distinct learner decision.
