Here the key response is checking activity rather than an advanced passer, with no new tactical decision before the gain.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rh6 pins f6 to Ke6 and makes fxg5 illegal. Removing the h6 rook allows fxg5 and loses a rook for a pawn (-400 cp).
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 21 roots compared, with no mate in one or forced mate in two. Rxf6+ Kxf6 and Rxh4 Rxh4+ lose material. Rh7 requires delayed manoeuvring.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 14 replies retain the pawn, and there is no legal capture of either rook immediately. An 850k check after Rf3+ Kh2 retains the pawn despite further checks. Deferral is about repetition of the decision.
reviewNotes.level: A direct Level A pawn capture, but too similar to the selected f-file version with more distinctive passed-pawn counterplay.
reviewNotes.provenance: Hong–Khubukshanov, World Rapid 2025, checksummed TWIC 1625. Exact ply 128 after Ke6 verified. Rxg5 was played.

deferred.reason: Bxg3 is sound, but ...Rd4 is a comparably strong and straightforward plan for a pawn gain without exploiting the pin. In supplemental 1M-node lines, ...Rd4 g5 hxg5 wins a pawn, and after Ra5 or Re2 the plan ...f6 puts White under enough pressure for ...hxg5 or ...Rxg4. That competing idea needs more than one solver move and was not proved against all replies, so preserve this as a reserve instead of rejecting it as a demonstrated universal bypass.
deferred.distinctness: A stationary rook pins a knight so the bishop can take a pawn. Kg2 releases the pin and the bishop can retreat, similar to other selected short king-release examples. The non-pin rook attack on g4 weakens the focus on the pin.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Without Rd1, White’s Nxg3 changes the +100 cp pawn gain to −230 cp and leaves no Black capture. The actual Bxg3 specifically relies on the pin.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 30 starts checked. The direct Bxg3 and ...Rd4 have almost equal root scores. Rd4 misses a next-turn gain against Ra7, Ra5, Re2 and other replies, but subsequent ...f6 leads to simple material in several deeper lines. No positive mate lead.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 17 first replies retain +100 cp and neither participant can be captured. Strong Kg2 and Re2 maintain the pawn gain in independent 1M-node probes, allowing a bishop retreat and ordinary rook counterplay. Deferred for competing plans rather than a tactical failure of Bxg3.
reviewNotes.level: A mechanically, but less focused than the chosen alternatives.
reviewNotes.provenance: Gilfanov–Remizov, Russian Blitz Championship, 2025-10-14. Exact TWIC 1615 full game after 57.g3 at ply 113, with played 57...Bxg3. FM and IM in source, archive checksum present.

deferred.reason: Qxh4 wins the knight and the tempting Rxh4 releases the pin, but the exact Qxh4, rook pin on g3, and king on g2 already occur in published f912718ed489d4e7. The alternative choice of capturing rook is useful but also covered separately by existing two-piece capture-choice examples. Prefer a different mechanism in the current batch.
deferred.distinctness: Compared published f912718ed489d4e7 Qxh4, the target is a knight instead of a queen, and Rg4 can also capture h4 but releases g3. The key pin and exact winning square are shared.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rg4 pins Pg3 to Kg2. Without the pinner, gxh4 takes the queen and leaves Black down 580 cp with no retake.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 23 roots and no mate within three. Rxh4 gxh4 loses the exchange by moving the pinner. Qxh4 is the only direct safe material gain.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Neither Qh4 nor Rg4 can be captured immediately. Qxe5 fxe5 takes the white queen and Rxd6 Bxd6 takes the white rook, both restoring more than the offered pawn. The strong c4 Qh5 branch retains the knight gain.
reviewNotes.level: A one-move gain tactically fits. Held for comparison with the published exact g-file decision.
reviewNotes.provenance: Elci–Volchkova, 1st 3-0 Thu 7th May 2026, complete checksum-bound TWIC 1644. Exact ply 59 after Kg2. Qxh4 was played.

deferred.reason: Both Rxg6 and Bxg6 exploit the same pinned knight for a clear pawn gain. The bishop route retains material under Bf6, so one capture would be an ambiguous learning choice in this collection.
Sound reserve. The current scope uses a more distinct decision in this teaching family.
deferred.distinctness: Both the pawn and its own queen attack the same pawn on g5. Capturing with the queen releases the pin and loses it. Capturing with the pawn keeps the diagonal pin, which contrasts with other cases where the pinner cannot even make the capture.
deferred.solutionVi: hxg5 — Tốt trắng từ h4 bắt tốt ở g5. Hậu f5 vẫn ghim Xe g6 vào Vua h7. Nếu Trắng chơi Qxg5, Xe g6 sẽ hết bị ghim và có thể bắt Hậu bằng Rxg5.
hintsVi: Cả tốt h4 và Hậu f5 đều có thể bắt tốt g5.
Nước bắt nào giữ được đòn ghim trên đường chéo f5–g6–h7?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Qf5 pins Rg6 to Kh7. Removing the queen makes Rxg5 legal, immediately erases the pawn gain and leaves no White recapture.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 28 legal roots compared, with no mate in one or forced mate in two. Qxg5 Rxg5 loses the queen despite the follow-up hxg5. Qxg6+ Kxg6 also loses the queen for a rook. g4 Kh8 f4 gxf4 is a slower exchange, not a simpler gain.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 11 legal replies retain the pawn and offer neither the moving pawn nor queen. Strong Rg7, Rd8 and h4 continuations retain +100 or better through active rook play. No recapture on g5 is legal after the root.
reviewNotes.level: One direct capture from equal material, no sacrifice. The visible queen capture is an instructive losing alternative.
reviewNotes.provenance: Sarana–Taher, 3rd 3-0 Thu 11th Dec 2025, checksummed TWIC 1623. Full replay verifies exact ply 216 after Rg6. hxg5 was played.

deferred.reason: Rxd5 is a sound reserve but repeats the exact pinned pawn e6, king c8 and capture square d5 of published Qxd5. This version uses a rook instead of a queen. The h6 line also needs care because the strongest Nf7 PV briefly loses the entire material gain before a technical rook exchange restores it. A quieter Ne4 is sound, but the available distinctness does not justify selecting it over clearer examples.
deferred.distinctness: Published 0decb450c568582e already uses the same diagonal through e6 to Kc8 to capture the pawn on d5. Here Kc7 allows a rook retreat and different later exchanges, but the original learner decision is nearly identical.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Without Bg4, exd5 becomes legal and turns the gain from +100 cp to −400 cp. Nxh7 only recovers 100 and allows ...Nxh7.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 36 legal roots compared. h4 Kc7, c4 d4 and Bh5 Re7 do not force a direct gain. No positive mate score.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 17 first replies retain +100 cp and neither participant can be captured. Kc7 Rd2 is a sound retreat confirmed in supplemental 1M-node analysis. Against h6, the stronger Nf7 line has temporary material recovery and a quieter Ne4 line is available. This is a reserve based on overlap, not an illegal line.
reviewNotes.level: A direct root, but other candidates add a more distinct decision and simpler practical payoff.
reviewNotes.provenance: Voitovich–Nguyen Ngoc Truong Son, 2nd 3-0 Thu, 2026-01-01. Exact TWIC 1626 replay after 18...Nf8 at ply 36. The played move was 19.Rxd5. FM White and GM Black in source, archive checksum retained.

deferred.reason: fxg4 is a clean pawn win but is a close duplicate of the published Sabria Batlle–Yang gxf5. In both positions a bishop on a long diagonal pins a pawn to the king, letting the adjacent pawn take without being recaptured. An advanced g-pawn supplies additional urgency here, but the exact learner decision is already represented.
deferred.distinctness: Compared published baaed4a0f0dced28 gxf5. The new black king often releases the f5-pawn, letting White take it as well, but the starting decision is the same pawn-on-pawn capture enabled by a bishop pin.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Bd3 pins Pf5 to Kg6. Removing Bd3 makes fxg4 legal and leaves the net gain at zero, with no White retake.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 16 roots compared with no mate within three. Bxf5+ Kxf5 loses the bishop for a pawn. The other roots leave Black active on the kingside.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All ten responses are non-captures and neither the bishop nor pawn is offered. Strong king moves like Kf7 allow Bxf5, which adds a pawn rather than returning the gain.
reviewNotes.level: Direct non-sacrificial capture qualifies tactically. Hold for overlap with the published pawn choice.
reviewNotes.provenance: Lazavik–Sarana, Titled Tue 13th Jan 2026, complete checksum-bound TWIC 1628 game. Exact ply 102 after ...hxg4. fxg4 Kf7 Bxf5 was played.

deferred.reason: Bxf6+ Kxf6 Bxd5 starts with an equal bishop-for-knight trade and then takes a bishop for nearly the same incremental gain. The engine prefers the direct pin line, but the simpler rival trade weakens the teaching decision.
Sound reserve. The current scope uses a more distinct decision in this teaching family.
deferred.distinctness: The queen stays on the open g-file to pin a pawn and the rook takes a full knight across the neighboring file. The opponent can attack a different pawn with Bxh6 or offer an equal rook trade on e3, rather than capturing the moving rook or pinner.
deferred.solutionVi: Rxf3 — Xe đen từ f8 bắt Mã ở f3. Tốt trắng g2 không thể bắt lại vì sẽ để Hậu g6 chiếu Vua g1. Nếu Trắng đáp Bxh6, trong phương án phân tích Đen bắt lại bằng gxh6.
hintsVi: Quan sát cột g từ Hậu g6 đến Vua trắng g1.
Tốt g2 có thể rời cột g để bắt Xe ở f3 không?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Qg6 pins g2 to Kg1. Without Qg6, gxf3 is legal and the rook is lost for a knight (-180 cp), with no immediate Black recapture.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 41 legal roots compared, including exact negative mate-in-one and forced-mate-in-two checks. c5 and Rf7 offer no direct gain. Qxg2+ Kxg2 and Qxe4 Rxe4 lose the queen.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 26 replies preserve at least +220 cp immediately. Neither Rf3 nor Qg6 can be captured. The sole capture Bxh6 is met by gxh6, and strong Re3 Rxe3 Rxe3 is a normal rook trade that keeps the knight gain. The other strongest rook moves do not recover the knight.
reviewNotes.level: One direct, nonsacrificial capture in an otherwise balanced position. Ordinary exchanges and the alternate capture on h6 do not recover the gain.
reviewNotes.provenance: Perez Gormaz–Dreelinck, 2nd 3-0 Thu 12th Feb 2026, checksummed TWIC 1632. Exact ply 31 after Rae2. Rxf3 was played, followed by Ng3. Bxh6 gxh6 is a separate analysis.

deferred.reason: Rxe5 really wins the pawn initially, but the most relevant defences leave a narrow material edge that depends on further rook manoeuvring. The 1M-node line after Kg7 Re6 Rd8 is only about +115 cp, and one sound-looking continuation allows ...dxe5 and returns the original pawn. The better Rb7 line needs Re6+ Rf6 Rxf6+ Kxf6 before settling. It overlaps the closely related existing reserve Garcia Correa–Herrera Rxe5.
deferred.distinctness: Both positions use the left-hand rook on rank six to pin d6 to Kg6 so Rh5 can save itself by capturing on e5. The later rook manoeuvre and presence of bishops are the main differences, rather than the learner’s initial decision.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Without Ra6, dxe5 becomes legal, turning the +100 cp pawn gain to −400 cp with no White capture.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 34 starts compared. Rh6+ Kg7 is not a material shortcut, and Rxd6+ permits Bxd6 or Kxh5. No positive forced-mate lead.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 27 replies retain +100 cp immediately. Neither involved rook is legally capturable. Supplemental 1M-node comparisons of Kg7, Rb7 and Rh8 find positional play favourable, but the strongest practical lines require further manoeuvring and close control of recovery.
reviewNotes.level: Direct at the root, but too similar to another reserve and technically marginal for this A batch.
reviewNotes.provenance: Shuvalova–Sai, Titled Tue, 2026-04-14. Complete TWIC 1641 replay reaches 34...Kg6 at ply 68 and the game played 35.Rxe5. Both IM in source, archive checksum present.

deferred.reason: Sound reserve. The current scope uses a more distinct decision in this teaching family.
deferred.distinctness: The pinner and the front bishop sit on the eighth rank. When the king leaves the pin towards e7, White can keep the gain by liquidating all four major and minor pieces.
deferred.solutionVi: Bxb6 — Tượng trắng từ d4 bắt tốt ở b6. Xe a8 ghim Tượng d8 vào Vua f8, nên Đen không thể đáp Bxb6. Trong ván đấu, sau Ke7, hai bên đổi Xe và Tượng bằng Rxd8 Rxd8 Bxd8+ Kxd8. Trắng giữ được phần vật chất vừa thắng.
hintsVi: Xe a8, Tượng d8 và Vua f8 nằm trên cùng hàng nào?
Nếu Tượng d4 bắt tốt ở b6, Tượng đen có thể rời d8 để bắt lại không?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Removing Ra8 permits ...Bxb6 and loses the capturing bishop. In the actual position it would expose the king.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 27 starting moves compared. Rxd8+ Rxd8 Bxb6 drops the exchange, Bxg7+ Kxg7 loses a bishop for a pawn, and the quiet bishop retreats concede the opportunity.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 20 legal replies keep the +100 increment on that turn. No legal capture targets either participant. After Ke7, the played Rxd8 Rxd8 Bxd8+ Kxd8 retains the pawn increment after even exchanges. ...Ke8 Kh2 and ...Rd1+ Kh2 were also checked; ...Rd1+ does not force material recovery.
reviewNotes.level: Direct pawn win without preparation or a sacrifice. An even liquidation is shown as optional follow-up.
reviewNotes.provenance: Mahdavi–Mekhitarian, 2nd 3-0 Thu 5 Feb 2026, checksummed complete TWIC 1631. Exact ply 70 after ...Rxd7. 36.Bxb6 Ke7 and the exchanges were played.

deferred.reason: Sound reserve. The current scope uses a more distinct decision in this teaching family.
deferred.distinctness: Both knights can reach c5, but the stationary rook pins only the defender. The strongest reply is a rook check that wins a pawn. Then the pin is released and the two knights can be exchanged without surrendering the bishop gain. This differs from taking a pawn with a knight pinned by a bishop.
deferred.solutionVi: Nxc5 — Mã từ b7 bắt Tượng ở c5. Xe c7 ghim Mã d7 vào Vua e7, nên Đen không thể đáp ...Nxc5. Trong ván đấu, Đen phản công bằng ...Rxb2+, bắt được một tốt.
hintsVi: Cả hai Mã đều có thể nhảy tới c5 theo cách đi của quân Mã. Hãy kiểm tra hàng bảy.
Nếu Mã d7 rời ô đó, đường chiếu nào sẽ mở ra?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Without Rc7, Black’s Nxc5 becomes legal, reducing the gain from +330 cp to +10 cp. White has no immediate capture. The bishop-for-knight exchange would not give the stated material gain.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 21 legal roots compared. Rxd7+ allows Kxd7, Rxc5 allows Nxc5, and quiet moves such as e5 allow the bishop to escape via Bb6 or the knight on b7 to be captured. No simpler material or mate bypass.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 24 first replies retain at least +230 cp and neither participant can be captured immediately. Strong Rxb2+ Ke3 Kd6 Rxd7+ Kxc5 is an ordinary exchange of knights and retains +230 cp. Separate 1M-node checks after the countercheck, Kd6 and the exact combined line confirm it. Kd6 as an immediate reply also allows Rxd7+ while maintaining the full bishop gain.
reviewNotes.level: A. Direct non-sacrificial capture from a material deficit. The checking reply only reduces the gain by a pawn, and there is a clear safe defence.
reviewNotes.provenance: Hong–Aryan, Saint Louis Masters, 2026-02-28. Both GM in TWIC 1634 archive. Exact full replay after 26...Bxc5 at ply 52, played 27.Nxc5 Rxb2+ 28.Ke3 Kd6 29.Rxd7+. Archive checksum verified.

deferred.reason: Sound reserve. The current scope uses a more distinct decision in this teaching family.
deferred.distinctness: Published Mester–Shevchenko Rxe5 also takes a rook guarded by a bishop-pinned pawn. Here the queen captures, and the decisive follow-up is stopping an outside pawn one step from promotion and then trading queens without returning the rook.
deferred.solutionVi: Qxe4 — Hậu từ f3 bắt Xe e4. Tượng b3 ghim tốt d5 vào Vua f7, nên Đen không thể bắt lại bằng dxe4. Trong ván đấu, Đen đẩy h2 và Trắng đáp Rh1 để chặn tốt h.
hintsVi: Tìm đường chéo từ Tượng b3 đến Vua f7. Tốt nào đang đứng trên đường này?
Nếu Hậu bắt Xe e4, tốt d5 có thể bắt lại mà vẫn che được Vua không?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Bb3 pins Pd5 to Kf7. Removing Bb3 makes dxe4 legal and leaves White down 400 cp from the adjusted start with no retake.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 49 legal roots compared with no forced mate in at most three. Rxd5 cxd5 concedes an exchange and needs more moves to recover. That line exploits a new pinned pawn on d5 to win some material but is neither direct nor non-sacrificial. Bxd5+ cxd5 and Rxf6+ Nxf6 also give material back.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 27 first replies are non-captures, so the queen and pinner are safe. h2 Rh1 stops the passed pawn immediately, as played. Ne7 Rf4 h2 Rh1 Qxe4 Rxe4 is an equal queen exchange that retains the rook. Rf4 safeguards the queen and moves the rook away from the knight attack.
reviewNotes.level: The gain is a direct one-move rook capture without a sacrifice. Stopping h2 or exchanging queens comes after the gain.
reviewNotes.provenance: Roebers–Mammadova, World Blitz Women 2025, complete checksum-bound TWIC 1625 game. Exact ply 66 after ...h3. Qxe4 h2 Rh1 was played.

selectionNotes: The published group includes both colors and rook, bishop, knight and pawn targets.
Haug–Tari is a sound reserve because Bulmaga–Schulze covers the same five-piece transition to king and pawn and includes the king recapture in the actual game.
Three original positions fill the remaining slots with an opposite-color bishop defence, a check after an attack on the pinner, and two bishops covering the pin and promotion square.

A.source: Complete indexed TWIC games. Every selected solving move was played. Any illustrative alternatives are identified separately.
teachingFamilies: Pin removes a recapture on a rook, bishop, knight, queen or pawn
King unpins the defender by moving or castling
Pinned defender still attacks a square the opposing king may not enter
Safeguard the material gain against an advanced pawn, a countercheck or an even exchange
A.exclusions: Withhold incidental pins, independent equal or simpler gains, short material recovery, sacrifices and repeats of published decision patterns.

publishedExerciseReviews.source: Active protected Pin catalog order at the start of review

decisions.reason: Qxf6 Qxf6 Bxf6 is the played line. The ordinary queen exchange retains a clean knight gain (+320) and bypasses the saved h7 promotion line. The 1.4M-node reply screen also checked Rb1+, Qc7 and Qe8.
decisions.reasonVi: Trắng có thể thắng Mã ngay bằng Qxf6 Qxf6 Bxf6, qua một lần đổi Hậu.

decisions.reason: Kg2 is the only king evasion keeping the advantage. Nxd4 Rc8+ Re8 Bxe8 Qd5+ Kh3 Rxe8 immediately reverses the nominal gain to −160, and White needs Rxe8+ Kxe8 Qxg7 to recover it. The minimum against all significant defences and the voluntary nature of the initial bishop loss remain unresolved.

Rb8 and Rxd7 really create the b-file pin and Qxa3 is the only clear gain in the short line. However, the 1.4M-node Rd2 reply leads to Qb4 Qxe5, immediately recovering the pawn. The compensation relies on the a-passer and a longer unsettled major-piece line.

After Qg8+ Nf7 the only comparable non-sacrificial route is Re1+. Qe5 interposes and the knight is pinned to the king, preventing Nxe5 when White takes the queen. Both legal recaptures Kxe5 and fxe5 leave a +400 gain. Re3+ needs a longer forced exchange; no simpler two-move gain against Nf7 was found in the 1.4M-node probe.
decisions.reasonVi: Mã chặn chiếu bằng Nf7. Cần tính thêm Re1+ Qe5 rồi Rxe5+ để thắng Hậu đổi Xe.
decisions.solutionVi: Phương án phân tích. Qg8+ buộc Đen chọn cách đỡ chiếu. Sau Nf7, Re1+ khiến Hậu đen phải chặn đường chiếu hoặc Vua phải đi. Nếu Đen đáp Qe5, Trắng chơi Rxe5+. Mã f7 bị Hậu g8 ghim vào Vua e6, nên không thể bắt lại. Sau Kxe5 hoặc fxe5, Trắng thắng Hậu đổi Xe.
hintsVi: Dùng Hậu chiếu trên đường chéo g8–e6.
Sau Nf7, tìm nước chiếu bằng Xe khi Mã đen đang che đường chiếu.

decisions.reason: The saved branch Rf1 Rg3 Qe2 Bxh3 gains a pawn, but after the played Qf2 Bxh3 the legal gxh3 gives a mating attack, and the stronger Re2 Rg3 Kg1 Rxf3 wins by a different exchange. Bg4 is also close to the saved root. The same short material objective under these defences remains unclear.

After Kc1 Ne7, the essential Nf5 offers a knight to Nxf5. The 1.4M-node branch gives mate in two after the offer and the saved Rxg7 returns the knight after Nxg7. The declined offer needs separate sacrifice-level treatment before using a starred grade.

Qh2+ Kf1 Qh1+ Ke2 uses simple consecutive checks to align Re4–Be3–Ke2, making Bxc1 illegal after Qxc1. The strongest replies preserve the rook gain, including an ordinary queen exchange after a5 Qc4+. The saved second move Qh1+ is analysis, the game played Bf4.

Bxa3 is a direct unpinned capture. The exact short capture gate retains a pawn through legal replies and recaptures on the short horizon. The strongest tested 1.4M branches Qd3, Qd2, Rg2 and Bf4 do not force immediate recovery and provide a much simpler material gain than Bc5 d4 dxe3.
decisions.reasonVi: Đen có thể bắt ngay tốt a3 bằng Bxa3 mà không cần đòn ghim ở e3.

decisions.reason: The simpler bxa5 is at least as strong as Na7. Ka8 allows a6 with the pawn held, while Bxa5 recovers it and White must create different threats with Reb1 or Nd6. The Na7 line also allows Rg8 and longer counterplay. No clear replacement or independent gain was established across these replies.

Qxf4 is an independent pawn capture. The all-reply short gate confirms the gain, and the stronger Kg2 continuation keeps it. The saved Bc6–Rxd3 line first trades queens and then wins a pawn through the relative pin, with later Rxc6 recovery to settle.
decisions.reasonVi: Đen có thể bắt ngay tốt f4 bằng Qxf4. Phương án Bc6 dài hơn và cần tính thêm phản công ở c6.

decisions.reason: The four-move main branch f5 Rxa3 fxe4 Ra7+ Kf6 Rxe4 Rxf3 leaves +230 and deeper checks retain the gain. Against Rxa3, early Bxe4 Rxe4 fxe4 Bxe4 gives only +70 and f4 allows Rc3 and material recovery. The new e4-pawn attacks the bishop pinned to Re3, and Bxe4 instead of Rxe4 exposes the rook to ...Rxe3. The a3-pawn was already attacked, and ...fxe4 immediately trades pawns. Against exf5 the f5-pawn can be retaken immediately with gxf5, but Bxf3 first wins the bishop and the pawn can still be recaptured. The local all-reply material search completed across all 41 legal roots (62,489 visits) and found no settled +100 gain in at most three solver turns.
decisions.reasonVi: Sau Rxa3, Đen cần tính fxe4, đáp nước chiếu Ra7+ bằng Kf6, rồi Rxf3 sau Rxe4.
decisions.solutionVi: Phương án phân tích. Sau f5 Rxa3 fxe4, tốt đen tấn công Tượng f3. Xe h3 ghim tương đối Tượng này vào Xe e3. Trắng có thể chiếu Ra7+, nhưng sau Kf6 Rxe4, Đen thắng Tượng bằng Rxf3. Nếu Trắng bắt tốt f5 ngay bằng exf5, Đen có thể bắt Tượng trước rồi bắt lại tốt f5.
hintsVi: Nhìn hàng 3 từ Xe h3 qua Tượng f3 đến Xe e3.
Nếu Trắng lấy tốt a3, tốt f5 có thể bắt ở ô nào để tấn công Tượng f3?

decisions.reason: After Nxd6+ Kf8 the nominal bishop gain is insufficient from −730 starting material. At 1.4M nodes Rf1 is the only favourable continuation. Against Nxe5, Qxe6 is the only favourable third move and the pin prevents fxe6. Qd5 Qf6 Rh7 does not force material recovery. Qxd6 is met by exd6, winning the queen. Rf1 never offers its own rook or knight for less material.
decisions.reasonVi: Sau Kf8, Trắng cần Rf1 để ghim tốt f7 rồi mới có thể bắt tốt e6 bằng Hậu.
decisions.solutionVi: Trong ván đấu, Trắng đi Nxd6+ Kf8 Rf1. Xe f1 ghim tốt f7 vào Vua f8. Sau Nxe5, Hậu trắng bắt tốt e6 bằng Qxe6 mà tốt f7 không thể bắt lại. Nếu Đen dùng Hậu bắt Mã ngay ở d6, Trắng có thể đáp exd6 để thắng Hậu.
hintsVi: Nước chiếu bằng Mã có thể đưa Vua đen đến cột nào?
Sau Kf8, tìm cách ghim tốt f7 trước khi đưa Hậu đến e6.

decisions.reason: Rxe7 creates a real mating threat by pinning g7 to Kh7, as Bxd1 Qxg7# shows. After Rg8 Rdd7 Kh8 Rxg7, however, Qe5 attacks the queen and requires Rge7 Rxg4 Rxe5 to settle the trade. Rd2 is another strong branch, so the saved stopping point and minimum depth need separate work.

Qxh3 gxh3 is an equal queen exchange. Reg8+ makes Bg3 interpose, allowing Rxh4 because Bxh4 would expose Kg1. Kf2 Bc5+ and Rxe4 Rxe4 retain the gain. The alternative Rxe4 after Qxh3 permits Qxh2+ without any initial Black sacrifice.

The game line fxe4 Ng5 e3 leaves the stationary rook on e6 available to Nxe6. A 700k probe finds exd2 Rf1 Rxe6, with the rook first being given up and tactical compensation recovered afterward. After dxe3, Nxe6 can also lead to exd2+ and a promotion tactic. This is a real exchange offer in the prepared line, so the current nonsacrificial B claim and a starred regrade need a different verified line. The sample itself is from the game.

Black has stronger counterplay by declining with Rg2: Nxg7 Rxg7 wins the same exchange, and Qh4 protects the gain through the two main defences d5 Bf1 and Rg1+ Kb2. The pin freezes the rook while the single knight offer overloads e7; this is a simple C combination even though the teaching acceptance line has four White moves. The accepted line is analysis. decisions.solutionVi: Trong ván đấu, Trắng chơi Qxf4. Đen chen nước chiếu ...d4+ rồi bắt Hậu bằng ...gxf4 sau Kg1. Trắng chiếu Bxd4+ và Đen đưa Xe đến g7 để chắn. Tượng d4 ghim Xe g7 vào Vua h8, nên tốt h6 bắt Xe bằng hxg7+ và Trắng vượt lên về vật chất. Phương án phân tích. Nếu Đen bắt lại bằng ...Qxg7, Trắng có Bxg7+. Nếu Đen chắn bằng Hậu với ...Qg7 ngay sau Bxd4+, Trắng cũng chơi hxg7+. Nếu Đen bắt Hậu ngay bằng ...gxf4, Trắng tiếp tục Bd4+ Rg7 hxg7+. Sau ...Qxg7, Bxg7+ thu hồi thêm vật chất.
hintsVi: Sau Qxf4, hãy tính nước chiếu ...d4+ trước khi Đen bắt Hậu.
Tượng có thể chiếu trên đường chéo nào để buộc Đen đưa quân vào ô g7, nơi tốt h6 đang khống chế?

sacrifices.reason: White deliberately allows g5 to capture the queen on f4 after the countercheck. The immediate bishop capture does not recover the unequal loss, and the pinned rook is won two White turns after acceptance.

decisions.reason: Unresolved depth under a strong defence. The played ...Rxf2 Rxf2 ...Qg3+ Qg2 ...Bxf2+ is a genuine rook offer with a direct pin of Qg2 to Kg1. The equally credible Kh1 response to ...Qg3+ (+229 versus +257) avoids that pin and is much harder. A local all-reply check found no +100 settlement in two further Black moves. The leading ...Qxh3+ Kg1 ...Bxf2+ Kxf2 ...Rf8+ Bf4 ...Qxg4 still leaves a −30 nominal balance after six Black turns and leads to complex play. The short sample is insufficient for C and no fully verified longer pin payoff supports D/E.

Grade mismatch. Bg5 creates a genuine pin of Nf6 to Ke7, preventing ...Nxd7. The played Bg5 ...Bg7 Nd7 ...Rxd7 Rxd7+ immediately trades a knight for a rook and settles +180. ...Kf8 Bxf6 Bxf6 is an even follow-up exchange. The sacrificed-looking Nd7 is an ordinary recovered exchange; the game needs no further material recovery and does not qualify for D/E.

The actual Nxb5 ...cxb5 Qxb5+ loses a knight for two pawns and remains down 120 until the third White turn. Against best ...Nd7, Qb5 pins Nd7 to Ke8, making ...Nxc5 illegal and allowing Rxc5 to gain +210. Practical ...O-O and ...Rb8 preserve the advantage, and ...Qxh4 loses the queen to gxh4. The near-best decline ...Bxe3 permits Rxc6 ...Bxd2+ Kxd2 (+330); the alternative ...Bxf2+ is likewise met by Kxf2. The non-sacrificial Qa6 and Qb3 score comparably in long play but fail to settle even +100 in three total White turns against ...Qb6 and ...b4 respectively. No simpler material bypass survives those replies.
decisions.solutionVi: Trong ván đấu, Trắng thí Mã bằng Nxb5. Sau ...cxb5 Qxb5+ ...Nd7, Hậu b5 ghim Mã d7 vào Vua e8. Vì Mã không thể bắt lại ở c5, Trắng chơi Rxc5, lấy Tượng và vượt lên về vật chất.
hintsVi: Hãy tìm cách đưa Hậu đến b5 với nước chiếu.
Sau khi Mã Đen chắn ở d7, quân nào của Trắng có thể bắt Tượng c5?

decisions.reason: Unresolved pin necessity for a longer grade. The played Rdxe7 ...Rxe7 Rxg6+ ...Bg7 Bxg7 includes a genuine initial rook sacrifice, but the credible recapture ...Rxg7 erases the displayed +250. The recovery Rxg7+ ...Kxg7 Ne6+ ...Kf6 Nxd8 restores +420 only on White turn six. Exact local checks after ...Bg7 found no +100 settlement in three further White turns (6,462 calls), and the all-28-root continuation after ...Rxe7 had only Rxg6+ clearly ahead. However, after the pinned bishop is captured, ...Rxg7 remains legal, and the final gain comes from the knight fork. The fact that Rg6 prevents ...Kxg7 at Bxg7 does not establish necessity: a hypothetical immediate king recapture would put the king on g7 earlier, accelerating the fork. The game played ...Re2+ instead, and the near-best ...Rd5 has a different, shorter material recovery. No E line with an essential pin is established.

Grade mismatch. The played Nxd6 ...cxd6 Ne5+ ...Rxe5 Rxe5 and the saved reordered line give two knights for bishop and rook, settling +180. Rd1 genuinely pins the d6-pawn to Kd7 and prevents ...dxe5. The apparently offered knights participate in immediate recovery, and the strong c4 branch reaches the same exchange later. The correct motif does not need a complex accepted sacrifice or D/E depth.

The absolute e-file pin is real: Re1 against Ke8 rules out ...Nxd5 by the e7 knight. In the saved analysis 1.Nc3 Rd8 2.Nd5 Rxd5 3.Rxd5, the offered knight is immediately exchanged for a rook (+180 cp material) and no accepted sacrifice survives settlement. The source played 1.Nf4, which also reaches the mechanism. This is a lower non-sacrificial grade question, outside the current D/E transfers.

The played ...Nxb4 cxb4 is an accepted knight for a pawn, leaving Black 220 cp of material down relative to the start until ...Bh6 attacks Ne3. Qe4 pins Ne3 relatively to Re1 and backs the capture: after Kh1 ...Bxe3, Rxe3 is answered by ...Qxe3, leaving +170 cp even after Nxd6. The strong Qe2 and Ree2 are met by ...Bxe3+ and the best continuations retain the gain. White can move the knight to c4 or g4, but ...Qxc4 or ...Qxg4 still wins it. The closely scored ...Nd4 also offers the knight to cxd4 and invokes ...Bh6, and the next root ...Na7 Qh5 ...Rg7 Nxa7 ...Rxa7 Rf2 ...Rxa4 is slower and no simple bypass. However, 3.Qd2 Bxe3+ 4.Rxe3 refutes the direct ...Qxe3+ via Qxe3. The 3M-node follow-up ranks ...Qb1+ Re1 ...Rxg2+ Qxg2 ...Qxe1+ and ...Rxg2+ Qxg2 ...Qxe3+ highest, but the ensuing long attack eventually settles at only +40 cp material before later pawn trades. This specific material defence leaves no verified simple C payoff or supported D/E replacement.

The played 1.Nfxe5 Qe7 2.Rfe1 Bxe5 3.Nxe5 exploits the e-file, but the apparent loss from 3...Qxe5 is recovered in the same exchange by 4.Qxe5 Rxe5 5.Rxe5, settling at +290 cp material. If 1...Bxe5 immediately, 2.Nxe5 already retains the pawn (+110 cp), and 2.Rxd8 Rxd8 3.Nxe5 is another stronger response. The normal exchange and relative pin remain suitable for non-sacrificial review, but this is neither a required C sacrifice nor a D/E line.

The played ...Bxe6 Bxe6 ...Qb5+ Qd3 ...Qxb2 really gives up the bishop on e6, but the stronger direct ...Qb4 Qd3 ...Qxb2 wins the pinned bishop at b2 without a sacrifice, with +330 cp at the capture and +334 cp engine score on the strongest reply. The same relative Be5–Bb2–Ra1 pin restricts the target. The targeted screen included Rh4, Bd5 and Qd5, all no stronger than Qd3. This is a shorter same-motif solution and a lower-grade mismatch.

The played 1.Nxd5 Nxd5 2.e4 Bg7 3.exd5 gives a knight for a pawn before attacking d5. The d1 rook pins the recapturing knight on d5 relatively to Qd8, so a knight retreat off the file loses the queen to Rxd8+. The strongest ...Ngf6, ...Bg7, ...Qd7 and ...Bd6 allow exd5 for +100 cp, and 3...Bxd5 in the played branch is met by 4.Rxd5. The weaker ...Ngf6 3.exd5 Nxd5 4.Bxd5 Bxd5 is answered by 5.Qe2+ Qe7 6.Qxe7+ Kxe7 7.Rxd5 (+320 cp). The targeted alternative 1...Bxd5 2.e4 Bd6 3.exd5 gains +110 cp using the same pin. 1.Bxd5 meets 1...Nxd5, with no shorter independent gain verified, and 1.a4 Qb6 2.axb5 axb5 only delays the d-file tactic. The relevant strong defence permits the simple three-move recovery.

The Qh3–h7–Kh8 pin is essential because it prevents ...hxg6. In the saved 1.Bg6 Ndb8 2.Bxh7 Qxh7 3.Nxh7 Rxh7 (the source played 1...Nb6), the bishop and knight are exchanged for a queen and pawn in a continuous, favorable capture sequence (+350 cp). There is no accepted sacrifice after the h7 exchange settles. This is a valid non-sacrificial pin with a lower-grade mismatch.

1.Nxd6+ exd6 is a genuine knight offer, and 2.Qe2+ can absolutely pin a blockading bishop. The saved 2...Be6 3.Bxe6 does not settle the objective: the played and strongest 3...O-O needs further work, and 3...fxe6 4.Qxe6+ still leaves White 120 cp below the starting material balance. The near-strongest 2...Be5 requires a longer candidate line, e.g. 3.Rad1 Qc5 4.Rd5 Qc7 5.Rxd6 Qxd6 6.Bxe5 Qe7 7.Bxh8 Qxe2 8.Bxe2. 2...Kd7 and 2...Kf8 also need separate recovery lines. No short settled C payoff or verified full E replacement has been established.

1.Bxd4 cxd4 is an equal trade. In the saved analysis 2.Nxf5 Bxf5 3.Bxf5, even 3...Nxf5 is followed immediately by 4.Rxf5, restoring the full pawn gain (+100 cp). The source chose 2...Nxf5 directly. The f4 rook and f6 queen supply the relative pin, but the nominal knight loss vanishes when the f5 exchange is completed. The countercheck ...Re1+ is met by Kf2. No required accepted sacrifice is shown, so the current C grade needs lower non-sacrificial review.

The played 1.Rxc7+ Qxc7 2.Rxc7+ Kxc7 exchanges two rooks for a queen and pawn at equal material; 3.exd4 is then the extra pawn. 1.exd4 already wins that pawn directly. The deepest tested reply ...Nd5 2.Rc4 retains +100 cp through the practical reply sequence. 1.Qxd4 Qxd4 2.Rxc7+ Kb8 3.exd4 is a separate +200 cp line. The d4 pawn need not move or recapture before White takes it in the played sequence, so the d-file pin is incidental to the stated gain.
decisions.reasonVi: Trắng có thể bắt tốt d4 ngay bằng exd4 và vẫn giữ được tốt hơn trước nước đáp ...Nd5. Chuỗi đổi hai Xe lấy Hậu và tốt ở c7 không cần thiết để đạt mục tiêu, và đòn ghim trên cột d không quyết định việc bắt tốt.

decisions.reason: 1.Be4 Qe2 2.Nxd6+ Rxd6 3.Rxd6 gains a rook and pawn for a knight (+280 cp), with Qc3 pinning the c7 bishop to Kc8 to rule out ...Bxd6. The game played 1...Qg4. The strongest response 1...Qe2 leaves only the ordinary favorable recapture chain; the legal offer 1...Rxe4 is far weaker and does not make a sacrifice necessary. Lower non-sacrificial grade mismatch.

In the played ...Nxb3 Qxb3 ...a5 Rhf1 ...axb4, Black genuinely offers a knight for a pawn to lure the queen onto b3, where Qb7 with Rb8 pins the b4 bishop. The targeted ...axb4 also works against strongest Kb1 and the near-strongest h4 and g5, with +110 cp after a4. After the capture, White axb4 ...Bxb4 restores the same gain, and Qxb4 ...Bxb4 loses the queen. White can decline ...Nxb3, but that lets Black keep the captured pawn or win material elsewhere. The comparable engine root ...Ne4 Bxe4 ...dxe4 Bxf8 ...Rxf8 leaves only +10 cp from two normal exchanges, with no comparable short gain.

The all-legal tree proves exactly two mate-in-three roots, ...Qxg2+ and the played ...Rd1+, and no mate in one or two. After ...Qxg2+ White has only Qxg2, then ...Rd1+ forces Rf1 and ...Rxf1# finishes. In the played order ...Rd1+ Rf1 ...Qxg2+ Qxg2 ...Rxf1# reaches the same position. Against ...Rd1+, Qf1, Qe1 and Qxd1 all permit ...Qxg2#. Both full three-move lines accept the queen sacrifice. Removing Bb7 makes Qxf1 legal at the final position, proving the absolute pin is essential. The saved queen-first order is analysis, and the source used the rook-first order.

Preserve the owner-authored C line. After Rxb1, the rook on b1 pins Re1 to Kf1. The best Rxb1 accepts a real exchange loss for Black; Qf5+ checks before recovering, and all strong king replies allow Qxb1. The full-game reference resolves to the Fork source.

Rxd8 is strongest, but Qxc3 immediately recovers a queen for the rook, leaving at least +300 in the strongest fxe6 defence. The shared classifier therefore treats the loss as immediately recovered.
